newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Envoy exchange a new start in U.S.-Vietnam history.
newsitem.headline: Envoy exchange a new start in U.S.-Vietnam history.

text.p: The United States' first ambassador to Vietnam, Douglas "Pete" Peterson, arrived in Hanoi on Friday to take up his post, marking a new start in the two countries' recent history of stormy relations.
The following is a chronology of key dates in U.S.-Vietnamese relations since the mid-1960s.
1964 - United States, in support of the South Vietnamese government, launches air war against North Vietnam and imposes trade embargo against Hanoi.
1965 - United States sends combat troops to South Vietnam.
January 27, 1973 - Ceasefire agreement is signed in Paris, ending U.S. combat role in Vietnam.
April 30, 1975 - North Vietnamese forces take over Saigon, ending the war and reunifying the country. Washington extends embargo to all of Vietnam.

1978 - Vietnam's relations deteriorate with China and Beijing-backed Khmer Rouge government in Cambodia. Secret talks between Hanoi and Washington on normalising relations break down as United States concentrates on developing ties with Beijing. Vietnam signs friendship pact with Soviet Union.
December 1978 - Vietnam invades Cambodia and topples Khmer Rouge.
1979 - Western European countries and non-communist Asian nations support U.S.-led embargo against Vietnam, in protest against invasion of Cambodia.
1988 - Vietnam begins cooperation with United States to resolve fate of American servicemen missing in action (MIA).
September 1989 - Vietnam completes Cambodia withdrawal.
April 1991 - Washington presents Hanoi with "roadmap" plan for phased normalisation of relations and lifting of embargo. Both sides agree to open U.S. government office in Hanoi to settle MIA issue.
October 1991 - Vietnam supports U.N. peace plan for Cambodia. Secretary of State James Baker says Washington is ready to take steps towards normalizing relations with Hanoi.
December 1991 - Washington lifts ban on organised U.S. travel to Vietnam.

April 1992 - Washington eases trade embargo by allowing commercial sales to Vietnam that meet basic human needs, lifts restrictions on projects by American non-governmental and non-profit groups and allows establishment of telecommunications links with Vietnam.
July 2, 1993 - U.S. President Bill Clinton clears way for the resumption of international lending to Vietnam.
September 13, 1993 - Clinton eases economic sanctions against Vietnam to let U.S firms join in development projects.
January 27, 1994 - The Senate urges Clinton to lift embargo, saying this would help get a full account of MIAs.
February 3, 1994 - Clinton lifts trade embargo.
January 28, 1995 - United States and Vietnam sign agreements settling old property claims and establishing liaison offices in each other's capitals.
May 15, 1995 - Vietnam gives U.S. presidential delegation batch of documents on missing Americans, later hailed by Pentagon as most detailed and informative of their kind.
July 11, 1995 - Clinton announces "normalisation of relations" with Vietnam, saying the time has come to moved forward and "bind up our wounds" from traumatic war years.
Aug 6, 1995 - Secretary of State Warren Christopher visits Hanoi to seal new relationship and raise flag at new U.S. embassy.
Nov 7, 1995 - Former U.S. Defence Secretary Robert McNamara, a key strategist and architect of a war he now says was "terribly wrong", visits Hanoi.

July 12, 1996 - U.S. National Security Adviser Anthony Lake visits Hanoi to mark first anniversary of normalisation of relations and add zest to slow-moving economic and strategic ties, but stresses that MIA issue still tops Washington's agenda.

April 7, 1997 - U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Finance Minister Nguyen Sinh Hung sign accord in Hanoi under which Vietnam will repay the United States debts of around $145 million which it inherited from the former government of South Vietnam.
April 10, 1997 - U.S. Senate confirms Douglas "Pete" Peterson, a former Vietnam War veteran and prisoner of war, as ambassador.
April 16, 1997 - United States and Vietnam reach agreement on treaty providing legal protection for copyright owners.
May 6, 1997 - Vietnam's ambassador to the United States, Le Van Bang, leaves Hanoi for Washington.
May 9, 1997 - Peterson takes up post as ambassador in Hanoi.
